rulings.challenge_claim: 12:16's own bicolon reading is byte-true, but its claim that no other antithetic pair in the chapter carries a temporal qualifier is byte-false (counter-example: 12:19).
rulings.grounds: Independent re-derivation from bytes upholds the LF challenge. verse_map_oshb.json Prov.12.16 (byte tier) = "אֱוִ֗יל בַּ֭יּוֹם יִוָּדַ֣ע כַּעְס֑וֹ וְכֹסֶ֖ה קָל֣וֹן עָרֽוּם": the A-colon's בַּ֭יּוֹם ("in that day") is a genuine temporal qualifier. A full-chapter re-scan of all 28 verses of ch.12 (not just the LF-cited 12:19) for the temporal-qualifier class (day/forever/moment tokens, pointed-disambiguated) finds exactly ONE other hit: Prov.12.19 (byte tier) = "שְֽׂפַת אֱ֭מֶת תִּכּ֣וֹן לָעַ֑ד וְעַד אַ֝רְגִּ֗יעָה לְשׁ֣וֹן שָֽׁקֶר" -- "a truthful lip is established לָעַ֑ד (forever), but a lying tongue [lasts only] וְעַד אַ֝רְגִּ֗יעָה (a moment)" -- itself antithetic (web:Prov.12.19 carries WEB's own "but"), carrying TWO temporal tokens. A third candidate, 12:17's ve-ed shall not be counted: that word is the homograph tsere-pointed "witness" (root ayin-vav-dalet), not the patach/kamats "until/forever" word seen in 12:19 -- pointed disambiguation excludes it, so it adds nothing to the count. Digit-bearing, object-named sweep: 2 of ch.12's ~25 antithetic ("but") verses carry a temporal-qualifier token (12:16 with 1, 12:19 with 2); zero of the remaining ~23. The row's rationale clause "a temporal qualifier that the chapter's other antithetic pairs do not carry" is therefore byte-false as an unqualified universal -- 12:19 is a direct counter-example, matching LF's finding exactly. This does not disturb the row's actual single_proverb / no-cluster-with-12:15 call, which rests on the asyndeton/antithesis internal to 12:15 and 12:16 separately, not on chapter-wide uniqueness -- the defect is confined to the rationale/observed_substrate_signals prose. Distinct from the OL item on this same row (missing Hebrew quotation): that is a citation-completeness defect, this is a factual-accuracy defect in the claim itself; not a duplicate.
rulings.remedy: Author-wave work order on P06-016: in rationale, delete or rescope the clause "a temporal qualifier that the chapter's other antithetic pairs do not carry" (and the matching observed_substrate_signals entry if it keeps the comparative framing). Option A -- DELETE the comparative clause entirely; the single_proverb call does not depend on it. Option B -- RESCOPE to a true, digit-bearing, object-named statement, e.g. "12:16 is one of only two antithetic pairs in the chapter (2 of ~25) carrying a temporal-qualifier token -- the other is 12:19's forever/momentary contrast (לָעַ֑ד / וְעַד אַ֝רְגִּ֗יעָה) -- and the only one of the two adjacent to its rejected sibling 12:15." Test the cure must pass: a full re-scan of all 28 ch.12 verses for the temporal-qualifier class (pointed-disambiguated from the 12:17 witness homograph) must return exactly {12:16, 12:19} -- the same whole-chapter sweep that falsified the original unscoped claim, not a spot-check of only the neighboring verses.

rulings.challenge_claim: The temporal-qualifier-vs-concealment antithesis is byte-accurate and the shared fool-noun with 12:15 is properly disclosed, but the row quotes no Hebrew.
rulings.grounds: Independent re-derivation upholds the OL challenge. P06-016's four prose fields (rationale, rejected_alternative, observed_substrate_signals, device_notes) contain zero Hebrew-script characters; every original-language claim (the coordinating waw at the B-colon head, the same-day temporal qualifier, the shared fool-noun with 12:15) is stated in English gloss only, with zero quoted pointed forms across the row's 3 original-language claims (temporal qualifier, coordinating waw, shared fool-noun). OL's own byte citations for what SHOULD be quoted check out: Prov.12.16 (byte tier) = "אֱוִ֗יל בַּ֭יּוֹם יִוָּדַ֣ע כַּעְס֑וֹ וְכֹסֶ֖ה קָל֣וֹן עָרֽוּם" -- אֱוִ֗יל opens the verse and matches Prov.12.15's own אֱ֭וִיל (collate.py confirms both at tier=byte), בַּ֭יּוֹם is the temporal qualifier, and the B-colon opens וְכֹסֶ֖ה (waw + participle) exactly as the row's prose describes. This is a real gap against the toolkit standing rule ("Quote the original language for every boundary-relevant original-language claim") and matches OL's own systemic low-severity finding across 7 of the other 7 rows in cluster c10's OL packet (P05-063, P06-003, P06-005, P06-006, P06-007, P06-013, P06-015 -- 7 of 8 rows total including this one), all carrying the identical or closely-related no-quoted-Hebrew defect class -- not row-specific carelessness but a cluster-wide citation-completeness gap. Distinct from the LF item on this row (a factual-accuracy defect in the universal claim itself); both remedies land in the same rationale/observed_substrate_signals fields but fix different things and are not duplicates.
rulings.remedy: Author-wave work order on P06-016: splice (never hand-type) בַּ֭יּוֹם and וְכֹסֶ֖ה from verse_map_oshb.json Prov.12.16 into the rationale/observed_substrate_signals prose as quoted forms tagged oshb:Prov.12.16, replacing the current English-only "same day"/"coordinating waw" glosses. Test the cure must pass: collate.py --ref oshb:Prov.12.16 --quote '<inserted span>' returns tier=byte for every inserted Hebrew span (never nfd/skeleton) -- the same collate-tier check that exposed the absence.
